title: Functorial standard resolutions and comparison with arbitrary polynomial resolutions
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Let $F_A(E)=A[E]$ be the free polynomial algebra on a set $E$, let $U$ forget an algebra to its underlying set, and let $P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(B/A)$ be the augmented simplicial algebra with $P^{\mathrm{std}}_n=(F_AU)^{n+1}B$; its faces are induced by evaluation $F_AU\to\mathrm{id}$ and its degeneracies by the unit $\mathrm{id}\to UF_A$. For a simplicial module $M$, write $s(M)^{-n}=M_n$ with differential $\sum_i(-1)^id_i$ and zero positive terms. Define $L_{B/A}=s(\Omega^1_{P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet}B)$ in $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with differentials as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. The standard augmentation is a resolution. Here a polynomial resolution $P_\bullet\to B$ means that every $P_n$ is a polynomial $A$-algebra surjecting onto $B$ and $s(P_\bullet)\to B[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For every such resolution there is a canonical comparison isomorphism $s(\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B)\simeq L_{B/A}$, natural for morphisms of augmented polynomial resolutions. A commutative square of ring maps $A\to B$, $A'\to B'$, $A\to A'$, $B\to B'$ induces a canonical semilinear map $P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(B/A)\to P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(B'/A')$ commuting with the augmentations, hence a map of differential complexes. These standard maps preserve identities and compose strictly; the induced maps in derived categories agree with the maps obtained using polynomial resolutions and their canonical comparisons.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-augmentation-boundary] to $A\to B$. Its standard simplicial algebra has precisely the stated terms and operators, is termwise polynomial and surjective, and its alternating augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Its criterion also makes every polynomial resolution $Q$ of the statement a trivial Kan fibration over $B$.

proof.text: Choose the universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ of [lem-trf-polynomial-presentation-homology] with $A$, $B$ and all the resolutions in question $\mathcal U$-small, so that every term lies in $\mathcal D_{B/A}$. For these augmentations apply [lem-trf-polynomial-presentation-homology] with $R=B$ and $F(T)=\Omega^1_{T/A}\otimes_T B$. The functor sends $\mathrm dx\otimes b$ to $\mathrm d(vx)\otimes b$; its existence and composition follow from [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Write $H=\mathbf H(\mathcal D_{B/A},F)$ and $K(Q)=s(F(Q))$. We obtain $a_Q:K(Q)\simeq H$ and $a_P:L_{B/A}\simeq H$. Set $c_Q=a_P^{-1}a_Q$. The cited naturality gives $c_RK(h)=a_P^{-1}a_RK(h)=c_Q$ for every resolution map $h:Q\to R$. In particular $c_P=1$.

proof.text: For a ring square, [lem-trf-polynomial-square-bar-naturality] gives the recursive standard map $t$, its strict identity and composition laws, and the indicated differential maps. Its comparison identities are $a_{Q'}K(h)=H(\alpha,\beta)a_Q$ and $a_{P'}K(t)=H(\alpha,\beta)a_P$, with target scalars restricted. Substituting $c_Q=a_P^{-1}a_Q$ yields $c_{Q'}K(h)=K(t)c_Q$. For arbitrary choices of endpoint resolutions, the transported map is therefore $c_{Q'}^{-1}K(t)c_Q$ and agrees with every supplied $h$. Identity, composition and transitive change of resolution follow by cancelling adjacent $c_Qc_Q^{-1}$ and using the strict laws for $t$.
